newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai copper ends up on LME gains.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai copper ends up on LME gains.

text.p: Shanghai copper futures ended up in slow trade on Thursday due to overnight gains on the London Metal Exchange but long liquidation and fresh selling pushed prices off highs, traders said.
The most active February 1997 contract ended at 19,000 yuan ($2,288) per tonne, up 210 yuan. It opened at an intra-day low of 18,950 and hit a high of 19,070.
November rose 150 to 18,700 yuan per tonne, December 100 to 18,700, January 150 to 18,930, March 170 to 19,080, April 110 to 19,110 and May 30 to 19,080.
Combined volume fell to 48,970 tonnes from 66,090.
Copper opened higher but profit-taking and short selling pushed prices off their intra-day highs but still up from Wednesday's close.
Traders said Shanghai investors were wary after an overnight breakthrough of the key $1,970 resistance level on the LME, down from an intra-day high of $2,000.
"Despite later-maturing contracts holding above the key 19,000-yuan support level, many investors were wary of the future trend," one trader said.
"Copper consolidated around 19,000 yuan late in the session, which made many players lose short-term direction," he added.
Traders said LME's movement tonight would influence that of Shanghai copper in the short term due to a lack of domestic market-moving news.
"Copper will test the 19,500-yuan resistance level if it breaches the key $2,000 resistance level on the LME, otherwise it will consolidate around 19,000 in the next few days," a second trader said.
Aluminium ended up. November rose 120 to 13,320 yuan per tonne, December 150 to 13,150 and January 100 to 13,100.
Combined volume fell to 490 tonnes from 1,210.
